A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DPA study. Their text, equations, six figures, references, and complete Appendix A support reliable comparison despite revised pagination.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original learned encodings for Gaussian data, a Gaussian mixture, and simulated Müller–Brown data, illustrated in Figures 2, 4, and 6.

after.justification: Section 4 retains these original empirical results, including polar-like encodings and approximate minimum free energy path recovery.

M1.justification: Both analyze the same DPA encoder and stochastic decoder with unchanged variability-minimization and joint energy-score objectives. Rewritten loss notation and additional decoder explanation do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same standard Gaussian, three-component Gaussian mixture, and Müller–Brown simulation scenarios. No additional empirical task or domain appears in the appendices.

E2.justification: Neither version reports an empirical evaluation of competing methods against DPA. The additional autoencoder comparisons in v2 Section 5 concern prior literature, not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Both retain 10,000 standard-Gaussian training points, identical mixture parameters, two-dimensional encodings, and treatment of Müller–Brown trajectory coordinates as i.i.d. samples. No revised evaluation protocol is reported.

E4.justification: The same three illustrative case studies are retained. Neither the main text nor appendices add ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness evaluations, or new empirical analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 2, 4, and 6 retain the same plotted encodings and color-bar values. The polar-like decomposition and single-encoding minimum free energy path findings remain unchanged; higher-resolution redisplays add no results.

T1.justification: The central results remain, with Proposition 3.3 relabeled Theorem 3.3. V2 locally revises Appendix A.1's delta-function derivation, corrects main-text moment expressions, and adds the cited asymptotic relation in Eq. 17. The rewritten exponential-family sum in Eq. 8 omits the component index on T.

C1.justification: The two central contributions remain. V2 removes the abstract's speculation about rivaling diffusion, explicitly claims improvements over prior autoencoder theory, and concludes that DPA provides an exact way to determine intrinsic dimensionality; v1 framed dimension determination as a prospective application.

C2.justification: V2 adds the tradeoff between latent dimensionality and score alignment in normal directions, and explicitly leaves proof of DPA's manifold-parameterization capacity to future work. It removes v1's scalar-potential explanation for approximately orthogonal encoding components.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 newly specifies default standard-Gaussian decoder noise with p−k components and explains input padding. V1 already used stochastic decoding and padding notation, so this is additional disclosure rather than evidence of changed implementation.

R1.justification: V2 adds a substantial related-work section positioning both contributions against denoising and contractive autoencoders, local moment matching, chart autoencoders, conditional VAEs, and disentanglement methods. Nine references are added while the original works are retained, replacing previously scattered comparisons with systematic research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 expands background explanations, revises the abstract and conclusion, and copyedits the main text and proofs. A dedicated related-work section absorbs the earlier VAE discussion, while the principal theory–experiments–appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: All six figures are retained with higher-resolution images but smaller displayed dimensions. Figure 1 is grouped with Figure 2 on page 7, and captions and page flow are adjusted. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: The new related-work section and expanded background make the theoretical contributions and setup easier to assess, providing a modest overall gain. The core evidence remains unchanged. Benefits are tempered by smaller plot labels, the indexing defect in Eq. 8, and stronger exact-dimensionality language without a corresponding demonstrated estimation procedure.
